title: Chapter 10: State Executive – Governor, Chief Minister and Council of Ministers

blocks.content: The Governor shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.

rows: Holds office during the pleasure of the President
Holds office as long as enjoying majority support in the Assembly
Aided and advised by the Council of Ministers
Heads the Council of Ministers and allocates portfolios

items: The Advocate General of the State is an integral part of the State Executive, whereas the State Election Commissioner and High Court judges are not.

Under the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act (2003), the total number of ministers including the Chief Minister cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly, with a minimum threshold of 12.
The Governor's ordinance-making power under Article 213 is co-extensive with the legislative power of the State Legislature and must be approved within six weeks from its reassembly.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The State Executive comprises the Governor, the Chief Minister, the State Council of Ministers, and the Advocate General of the State.
The Governor acts as the constitutional and nominal head (de jure), while the Chief Minister functions as the real executive head (de facto).
The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor, and other ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.
The State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State.
